title: 26 U.S.C. §4966 Taxes on taxable distributions
issuer: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
summary: 20% sponsor tax on taxable distributions; 5% (max $10,000) on fund managers agreeing knowingly; taxable = any distribution to a natural person, or to others unless charitable purpose and expenditure responsibility; exceptions for §170(b)(1)(A) orgs (not disqualified SOs), the sponsor, other DAFs; fund manager = officers/directors/trustees and employees with authority over the act.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4967 Taxes on prohibited benefits
issuer: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
summary: 125% tax on advising a distribution conferring more than incidental benefit on a §4958(f)(7) person (payable by advisor or recipient); 10% (max $10,000) on knowing fund managers; no §4967 tax where §4958 tax applies; joint and several liability.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4962 Abatement of first tier taxes in certain cases
issuer: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
pinpoint: §4962(a), (b); amendment note 2007 'substituted D, or G for or D'
summary: Qualified first tier tax (subchapters A, C, D, G, except §4941(a)) is not assessed/abated/refunded if the Secretary is satisfied the event was due to reasonable cause, not willful neglect, and corrected within the correction period. Subchapter G added in 2007.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4963 Definitions (first tier tax, second tier tax, taxable event, correct, correction period)
issuer: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
summary: First tier tax and taxable event lists include §§4966 and 4967; second tier list does not; 'correct' is defined by reference to the section imposing the second tier tax; correction period ends 90 days after a second-tier deficiency notice, extended by periods the Secretary finds reasonable.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4958 Taxes on excess benefit transactions
issuer: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
summary: Any grant, loan, compensation or similar payment from a DAF to a donor, donor-advisor, family member (4946(d) plus siblings) or 35% entity is an excess benefit in full; sponsor-compensated investment advisors are disqualified persons; correction of (c)(2) transactions may not be repaid into any DAF.

title: 26 U.S.C. §170 (b)(1)(A)(vii), (b)(1)(F), (b)(1)(I), (f)(18), (p)
issuer: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
summary: Private operating and certain conduit foundations are §170(b)(1)(A)(vii) organizations; 0.5%-of-contribution-base floor on itemized charitable deductions; DAF contribution deduction requires sponsor acknowledgment of exclusive legal control; nonitemizer deduction (p) excludes contributions to supporting organizations and to establish or maintain a DAF.

title: Chapter 42 subchapter structure (Subchapter G: Donor Advised Funds, §§4966-4967)
pinpoint: Chapter 42 table of subchapters
summary: Confirms Subchapter G = Donor Advised Funds (§§4966-4967), so §4962(b)'s reference to subchapter G covers §§4966(a) and 4967(a) taxes.

title: Notice 2017-73, Request for Comments on Application of Excise Taxes With Respect to Donor Advised Funds in Certain Situations (2017-51 I.R.B. 562)
pinpoint: §4 (pledge conditions 1-3), §3 (event tickets), §7 'Taxpayers may rely on the rules described in section 4 until additional guidance is issued.'
summary: DAF distribution to a charity to which the donor has pledged (enforceable or not) not a more-than-incidental §4967 benefit if the sponsor makes no reference to the pledge, no other more-than-incidental benefit, and no deduction claimed; §4967 only. Reliance until additional guidance.

title: REG-142338-07, Taxes on Taxable Distributions From Donor Advised Funds Under Section 4966 (NPRM), 88 FR 77922
effective_date: proposed; would apply to taxable years ending on/after publication of final TD
pinpoint: Preamble: Definition of donor; Distributions (fees, deemed distributions, anti-abuse intermediary rule); A. §170(b)(1)(A) orgs (ED); C.ii ER; fund manager; Proposed Applicability Date (reliance). Prop. §§53.4966-1(e),(f),(h)(3),(i); 53.4966-2(c)
summary: Not effective law but expressly reliance-eligible pending finalization. Defines fund manager incl. delegation; personal investment advisors as donor-advisors; public charities excluded from 'donor'; reasonable fees not distributions, donor-paid fund-specific expenses are deemed distributions; ED via 53.4945-5(a)(5)-like procedures; intermediary anti-abuse rule.

title: Federal Register document search: IRS documents matching 'donor advised funds' (newest first)
pinpoint: Results 1-20 of 27 (2026-11-24): latest §4966 items are 2024-01-09 comment extension, 2024-02-29 and 2024-04-19 hearing notices; no final rule or withdrawal
summary: As of 2026-11-24 the Federal Register shows no Treasury decision finalizing and no withdrawal of REG-142338-07; only the 2023 NPRM and 2024 procedural notices.

title: 2026-2027 Priority Guidance Plan (initial), Exempt Organizations item 4
issuer: Treasury / IRS Office of Chief Counsel
pinpoint: Exempt Organizations items 4 and 5
summary: Lists 'Guidance under §§4966 and 6033 regarding certain donor advised fund arrangements' and §6033 reporting guidance including fiscal sponsorship arrangements; no timetable.

title: 26 CFR §53.4945-5 Grants to organizations
pinpoint: (a)(5)(i)-(ii) good faith determination, currency, qualified tax practitioner; (a)(6)(i) earmarked grants; (b)(1)-(3) ER and written commitment; (b)(5) foreign restrictions; (c) reports
summary: ED ordinarily in good faith if based on current written advice received from a qualified tax practitioner and reasonably relied on; currency rule; secondary-grantee earmark rule (no named secondary grantee, no agreement to cause selection); ER signed commitment terms and reports.

title: 26 CFR §53.4941(d)-2(f)(2), (f)(9) incidental or tenuous benefit
summary: A disqualified person's incidental or tenuous benefit (e.g., as member of the public, from a qualifying scholarship program, or public recognition) is not by itself self-dealing.

title: T.D. 9740, Reliance Standards for Making Good Faith Determinations, 80 FR 57709 (preamble)
pinpoint: Preamble 'Reliance on Written Advice Shared by Another Foundation' (80 FR 57713-57714); 'Equivalency Determinations by Sponsoring Organizations of Donor Advised Funds' incl. fn 4 quoting JCX-38-06 p.349
summary: Shared advice may be used if reasonable under all facts and circumstances, but for the special (ordinarily-good-faith) rule the advice must be received from the qualified tax practitioner, not another foundation. DAF sponsors may use the regulations as guidance pending further guidance.

title: Rev. Proc. 2017-53 (equivalency determinations)
pinpoint: §2 (scope incl. DAF sponsors 'until further guidance'); §3.03(1) current advice; §3.03(2) qualified tax practitioner; §3.03(3) qualifying public charity / disqualified SO for §4966
summary: Guidelines for written ED advice; DAF sponsors may use for §4966(c)(2)(A); advice current while law unchanged and facts from grantee's current or prior taxable year (up to ~2 years); public support advice current for two years after the five-year test period.

title: Rev. Proc. 2018-32 (reliance on Tax Exempt Organization Search and EO BMF)
pinpoint: §1 purpose; §2 (grants under §§4942, 4945 and 4966); §5.01 general reliance; §6.01-.03 limitations (official name, listing, subordinates)
summary: Grantors may generally rely on TEOS/EO BMF public charity classification until public announcement of change, absent knowledge or responsibility; reliance limited to listed official names and not before listing.

title: Instructions for Form 4720 (2025)
pinpoint: 'Abatement' (p.6); 'Initial Tax Liability and Correction' (p.6); Who Must File; Schedule I (§4958); Schedule K (§4966); Schedule L (§4967); due date 15th day of 5th month
summary: Form 843 is used to request abatement under §4962 for first tier taxes including §§4966 and 4967; sponsors report §4966 on Schedule K; fund managers and donors/advisors file their own returns (Schedule L for §4967); §4958 is Schedule I.

title: Instructions for Schedule F (Form 990) (Rev. December 2024)
pinpoint: Part II line 1 columns (c)-(i), col (f) manner of cash disbursement; Part II scope incl. domestic org grants for designated foreign orgs; Regions list; continuous-use note
summary: Column (f): describe manner of cash disbursement such as cash payment, money order, electronic fund or wire transfer, check, other charges against funds on deposit at a financial institution, or other; list all that apply. Part II covers >$5,000 per recipient and grants to domestic organizations for designated foreign organizations.

title: T.D. 10056, Trump Accounts (temporary regulations), 91 FR 61705
pinpoint: Preamble E 'Tax Implications of Contributions'; Temp. Reg. §1.530A-7T(e)(1)-(2); Applicability Dates
summary: General funding contribution by a 501(c)(3), including via DAF, furthers exempt purposes, is a §170(c)(2)(B) purpose, is not a distribution to a natural person under §4966, and is treated as exercising ER; classes are broad and objective. Silent on §§4958/4967.

title: IR-2026-135 (nonitemizer charitable deduction reminder)
pinpoint: Paragraph on qualifying contributions
summary: 'Cash contributions made either to supporting organizations or to establish or maintain a donor advised fund do not qualify'; refers to Publication 6196.

title: Instructions for Form 8283 (Rev. December 2025)
pinpoint: Section B, Part V Donee Acknowledgment
summary: The donee organization that received the property must complete and sign Part V; signer must be authorized to sign the organization's returns or specifically designated.

title: About Form 8282, Donee Information Return
pinpoint: Purpose statement
summary: Donee organizations use Form 8282 to report dispositions of donated property within three years after the contribution.

title: IRS information letter 2024-0007 (UIL 170.07-07)
pinpoint: p.1-2 paragraph on earmarking/conduit
summary: States a taxpayer cannot deduct a donation to a US charity if earmarked for a foreign charity or if the US organization is merely a conduit; non-precedential.

title: Rev. Rul. 63-252 and Rev. Rul. 66-79 (control and discretion; conduit doctrine)
pinpoint: Holdings (not read in full text)
summary: Not fetched; known through search summaries: deduction allowed where domestic charity has control and discretion over funds and gift is not earmarked; a mere conduit makes the ultimate recipient the true donee. Verify full text before quoting.

title: Fidelity Charitable Program Guidelines (© 2026, CGF-PC-04/24)
pinpoint: Account Holder (charities not eligible); Contributions (costs associated with contributions; net proceeds); Eligible Grant Recipients (good standing federal and state; under investigation); Impermissible grants; Special purpose designation; Fees and Expenses
summary: Largest sponsor: charities cannot be account holders; contribution and selling costs allocated to the giving account; grantees must be in good standing under federal and state law; organizations reported as under government investigation treated as ineligible; non-binding special purpose designations; trustees may decline any grant.

title: Fidelity Charitable grant pledge help text
pinpoint: Pledge popup text
summary: A grant may satisfy a non-legally-binding commitment or pledge but not an enforceable (legally binding) pledge.

title: NGOsource 'Equivalency Determination on File' badge and repository model
pinpoint: Badge page (fetch failed; content seen only in search snippet)
summary: Search snippet: the badge means the organization was determined equivalent for a specific funder during a specific period; NGOsource reports many large DAF sponsors as members. Not verified by fetch.

title: California Attorney General, Registry of Charities and Fundraisers: Delinquency
pinpoint: Intro (citing Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11 §312); FAQ 6
summary: Organizations not in good standing (delinquent, suspended, revoked) may not operate or solicit donations in California, including not being listed in solicitations or receiving donations through charitable fundraising platforms.

title: Venable, Regulations Implementing California's Charitable Fundraising Platform law (AB 488)
pinpoint: Solicitation Types A-E; good standing verification
summary: CFP regulations cover platforms that solicit or recommend donations by listing charities by name (Type A) and SaaS giving software (Type E); platforms must confirm IRS, FTB and AG good standing for each recipient. DAF sponsors not discussed.

title: 8 Del. C. §141(a), (c), (j)
summary: Business and affairs managed by or under the direction of the board; board may designate committees exercising board powers per resolution/bylaws; nonstock certificates may vary management rules. Example of state law permitting delegation.

title: UPMIFA §3(c)(1) / state Uniform Prudent Investor Act cost standard
issuer: Uniform Law Commission; state enactments (e.g., HRS §554C-7)
pinpoint: UPMIFA §3(c)(1) (not fetched); HRS §554C-7 seen in search snippet only
summary: Fiduciaries may incur only costs that are appropriate and reasonable in relation to the assets, purposes and skills available. Text verified only via search snippets; confirm in the sponsor's state enactment.

title: California AG charities webinar citing Cal. Code Regs. tit. 11 §999.9.4
pinpoint: Slide citing §999.9.4 (search snippet only)
summary: Search snippet: registration must be current to operate; delinquent or suspended organizations may not solicit or disburse charitable funds. Not fetched.

title: 26 U.S.C. §4946(d) Members of family
issuer: Office of the Law Revision Counsel
summary: Family includes spouse, ancestors, children, grandchildren, great grandchildren and spouses of descendants (used by §4958(f)(4), which adds siblings).
